query: Sentence-level diff of Item 1A Risk Factors, LLY 10-K FY2024 vs FY2025 (full section dump, difflib); follow-up grep 'Bridge Program', 'cash-pay', 'insufficient to offset pricing' in 10-Q 2026Q2

candidate.text: Lilly's FY2025 10-K added a new risk that the volume gained from its U.S. government obesity deal may not cover the price concessions, and the Q2 2026 10-Q then revealed the Medicare access that volume depends on is a temporary Bridge program ending December 31, 2027 whose uptake is 'unknown'.

cites.quote: We continue to experience scrutiny on the pricing of current and potential diabetes, obesity, and Alzheimer's disease products due to payer concern over projected growth in these markets
cites.label: Eli Lilly 10-K FY2024, p. 26

cites.quote: Among other risks, we may fail to adequately capitalize on the additional U.S. access to our obesity medicines resulting from these agreements, particularly if the revenues generated from such expanded access are insufficient to offset pricing concessions.
cites.label: Eli Lilly 10-K FY2025, p. 27

cites.quote: Our financial results and prospects are subject to risks related to the level and pace of patient participation in cash-pay markets
cites.label: Eli Lilly 10-K FY2025, p. 27

cites.quote: Under the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge program (Bridge Program), Medicare beneficiaries obtained access to discounted Lilly obesity medicines effective July 1, 2026 through December 31, 2027
cites.label: Eli Lilly 10-Q 2026-06-30, p. 25

cites.quote: The uptake from this expanded access is unknown.
cites.label: Eli Lilly 10-Q 2026-06-30, p. 25

skeptic_materiality.round1: refuted=False severity=major. The wording is real. 10-K FY2025 p.27 adds the 'insufficient to offset pricing concessions' clause, which does not appear in 10-K FY2024 p.26. 10-Q 2026Q2 p.25 gives the Bridge Program dates as July 1, 2026 through December 31, 2027 and says 'The uptake from this expanded access is unknown.' The arithmetic is also right: -10% x $30,375M = $3,038M, and -5% x $19,304M (H1 2025 U.S., 10-Q p.28) = $965M. The problem is that the math touches the wrong price give-up. The 2025 U.S. price decline of 10% (10-K p.49) is attributed to Mounjaro and Zepbound generally. Most of 2025 came before the November 2025 preliminary agreement, and the Bridge only started July 1, 2026, after the 10-Q period ends. The H1 2026 -5% includes the 'previously announced reductions in cash-pay prices' (10-Q p.29). Q2 U.S. price was only -3% because a favorable rebate true-up worth 3% of U.S. revenue (10-Q p.10, p.28) offset it. So '~$1B per half-year price give-up' cannot be read as the deal's concession that the volume must offset. CORRECTION: Narrow to the disclosure change: a new 10-K clause admitting deal revenue may not offset concessions, plus a 10-Q end date for Medicare access. Do not size it with total U.S. price erosion. Most of the 2025 -10% predates the deal, and the Bridge's concession and volume both begin only in Q3 2026, so the deal's price cost is not yet visible in any filed period.
skeptic_materiality.round2: refuted=True severity=major. In round 1 I held the wording change and attacked the sizing. The obviousness skeptic's sources check out. The 2026-06 Lilly press release p.1 gives the Bridge end date ('December 31, 2027'; verify_quote true). The Q4 2025 transcript p.1 (grade C) has the CFO saying 'these price concessions will be more than offset by increased volume' (verify_quote true). So both legs were said in public. On my lens, nothing in a filed period carries a deal-specific number either: the Bridge started 7/1/2026, and the -10% (FY2025) and -5% (H1 2026) U.S. price lines are mostly pre-deal or cash-pay. That leaves no sizable, unsaid remainder. CORRECTION: Kill as a nugget. If the consensus angle is kept, it is a valuation view: I/B/E/S FY2028 EPS rose from $49.53 (2026-03-19) to $53.97 (2026-08-20), and that view relies on Medicare access that is guaranteed only through 12/31/2027. It is not a filing finding.

skeptic_obviousness.round1: refuted=True severity=fatal. Both legs are in Lilly's own press releases and prepared remarks. (1) Bridge end date: Lilly's 25 Jun 2026 press release says Bridge coverage 'begins July 1, 2026 ... and will run through December 31, 2027' (LLY:policy/press_2026-06_medicare_part_d_foundayo_zepbound.md p.1). On the Q1 2026 call (grade D) analyst James Shin (Deutsche Bank) asked 'With Bridge extending into 2027 ... is Lilly working ... to secure longer-term Medicare access?' and CEO David Ricks answered directly that the government is 'extending bridge', Part D plans did not opt in for 2027, and the 18-month window 'will then set up the '28 discussion' (LLY:transcripts/2026Q1_transcript.md p.1). The 10-Q p.25 sentence the candidate leans on just restates this. (2) Volume vs price give-up: CFO prepared remarks on the Q4 2025 call (grade C) guided 'Price is expected to be a drag on growth in the low to mid-teens', named the government access agreement as the first of three U.S. price factors, and said 'these price concessions will be more than offset by increased volume over time' (LLY:transcripts/2025Q4_transcript.md p.1). The Q2 2026 call repeats 'we are going to more than offset that with volume growth' (LLY:transcripts/2026Q2_transcript.md p.1). The 10-K risk-factor clause is the boilerplate mirror of a question management answers every quarter. (3) Consensus prices the volume-wins view: I/B/E/S FY2028 revenue mean rose from $107.6B (2026-02-19, 17 ests) to $113.8B (2026-08-20, 22 ests), and FY2026 from $82.1B to $88.3B (ibes_revenue_consensus.csv, LLY SAL rows). The candidate's 10-K-to-10-Q 'wording shift' is real but everything it reveals was already said in a press release and on a call. Transcripts are grade C/D, so these are evidence that the point was said, not quotable for the deck. CORRECTION: If kept at all, narrow to a contrarian view against consensus: I/B/E/S lifted FY2028 revenue about 6% in six months while the only Medicare obesity access Lilly has is a program its CEO says ends Dec 2027 with no Part D plan opt-in. That is a valuation view, not a filing find.
skeptic_obviousness.round2: refuted=True severity=fatal. Unchanged verdict. The materiality skeptic keeps c01 as a 'disclosure change'. But the two disclosures they keep, the Bridge end date and the volume-may-not-offset clause, are the two things Lilly said outside the filings: the 25 Jun 2026 press release ('will run through December 31, 2027') and Ricks on Q1 2026 ('set up the '28 discussion'). The CFO's Q4 2025 guidance named the government agreement as a price-drag factor and said 'more than offset by increased volume over time'. Their point that the deal's own concession is not yet in any filed period makes the obviousness case stronger: the only information investors have on it is guidance, and consensus took it (I/B/E/S FY2028 revenue $107.6B to $113.8B, Feb-Aug 2026). CORRECTION: Agree with their sizing fix. If the deck uses it, frame it as a consensus-vs-Bridge-expiry view, not as a filing find and not sized with the total U.S. price decline.

verdict_reason: Both skeptics refute in round 2. Obviousness: the Bridge end date is in Lilly's 25 Jun 2026 press release (LLY:policy/press_2026-06_medicare_part_d_foundayo_zepbound.md p.1), and the CFO said on the Q4 2025 call that price concessions 'will be more than offset by increased volume' (LLY:transcripts/2025Q4_transcript.md p.1, grade C, used as evidence it was said, not quoted). Materiality: the -10% FY2025 and -5% H1 2026 U.S. price lines (LLY:10k_FY2025.md p.49; LLY:10q_2026Q2.md p.28) mostly predate the deal, and the Bridge began 7/1/2026, after the 10-Q period. So no filed period carries a deal-specific number. The wording change itself is confirmed (LLY:10k_FY2025.md p.27 vs LLY:10k_FY2024.md p.26) but adds no unsaid fact. Confirmed killed, not merely unrefuted.

skeptic_materiality.round1: refuted=True severity=major. The claimed flip did not happen. 10-K FY2024 p.32 already says the risk 'may render built or in process manufacturing capacity unnecessary, and may also subject us to contractual payment obligations, which may be significant.' The same FY2024 paragraph also already says 'tirzepatide supply currently exceeds demand in the U.S.' The only FY2025 change (10-K p.34) is that 'overestimation of demand or' was inserted before 'events that limit demand.' That is a three-word edit, not a new warning. The PP&E figures check: 24,675/17,102 = +44.3% (10-K p.59), and 29,286/24,675 = +18.7% (10-Q p.7). The impairment sizing is a made-up 10% haircut, and its arithmetic is slightly off: 10% x $12,184M = $1,218M; x (1 - 0.199) = $976M; / 893.7M shares = $1.09/share, not $1.07. CORRECTION: Narrow to: FY2025 added 'overestimation of demand' to an existing overcapacity risk that already mentioned stranded capacity and significant contractual payments. No disclosed impairment or charge. PP&E +44% is a fact but not evidence of overbuild.
skeptic_materiality.round2: refuted=True severity=major. Both lenses reached the same finding: the FY2024 p.32 text already had the stranded-capacity and contractual-payment language. The other skeptic adds that FY2025 also inserted 'may result in supply imbalances', which is correct per 10-K FY2025 p.34. It also dropped the 2024 shortage example. Neither change carries a number. The 10% impairment remains an invented scenario. CORRECTION: Same as round 1. A three-phrase edit to an existing risk factor, with no disclosed charge.

skeptic_obviousness.round1: refuted=True severity=major. The candidate overstates the drift. The FY2024 10-K p.32 already says capacity build 'may render built or in process manufacturing capacity unnecessary, and may also subject us to contractual payment obligations, which may be significant' (LLY:10k_FY2024.md p.32). FY2025 p.34 only inserts 'overestimation of demand or' and 'may result in supply imbalances', and drops the 2024 sentence that 'demand for our incretin medicines exceeded production' (p.33 now has no shortage example). The capacity build itself is a prepared-remarks headline: Q4 2025 call 'We exceeded our goal to produce 1.8 times the number of incretin doses in 2025 ... we've committed over $55 billion, the largest manufacturing build-out in company history' (LLY:transcripts/2025Q4_transcript.md p.1); Q2 2025 call gave 1.6x first-half doses (LLY:companies/LLY/transcripts/2025Q2_transcript.md). No call I checked (2025Q3 B; 2025Q4, 2026Q1, 2026Q2 C/D) raises over-capacity, so the two-word insertion is not said elsewhere, but the PP&E growth it is paired with is the most visible fact about Lilly. Every incretin maker carries the same capacity bet (Novo), so it is also not company-specific. CORRECTION: Narrow to: FY2025 Item 1A added 'overestimation of demand' and 'supply imbalances' and removed the 2024 shortage example; the 'capacity unnecessary' and 'significant contractual payment' language was already there in FY2024.
skeptic_obviousness.round2: refuted=True severity=major. Both skeptics agree. On re-reading FY2024 p.32, it already says 'While tirzepatide supply currently exceeds demand in the U.S.', so the 2024 text already pointed in both directions. The FY2025 additions are 'overestimation of demand or' and 'may result in supply imbalances' (p.34); the materiality skeptic lists only the first. No call in all 10 Lilly transcripts in the index (2024Q1-2025Q2 grade C; 2025Q3 B; 2025Q4 C; 2026Q1 D; 2026Q2 C) uses over-capacity language. The capacity build ($55B committed, 1.8x doses) is in Q4 2025 prepared remarks. CORRECTION: FY2025 inserted 'overestimation of demand' and 'supply imbalances' into an existing stranded-capacity risk factor that already named significant contractual payments and already noted supply exceeding U.S. demand.

verdict_reason: Both skeptics refute in both rounds. LLY:10k_FY2024.md p.32 already says capacity may become 'unnecessary' with 'contractual payment obligations, which may be significant' and that 'tirzepatide supply currently exceeds demand in the U.S.'; LLY:10k_FY2025.md p.34 adds two phrases. No charge is disclosed and the 10% impairment is an invented scenario. The capacity build itself is a prepared-remarks headline. Confirmed killed.

One version is both material and not said in anything I checked: inventory keeps outgrowing cost of sales after launch. On the 10-Q 2026Q2 p.5 and p.7 and 10-Q 2025Q2 p.7, Q2 2026 inventory of 16,793 against annualized Q2 COGS of 13,072 gives 469 days, up from 410 days a year earlier (11,013.8 / 9,792). This is a cash-flow and write-down-risk item worth about 10% of FY2025 net income of $20.6B. It is not an EPS item unless written down. Management talks in doses produced (1.8x), not inventory days. CORRECTION: Kill the pre-launch and receivables framing. Pre-launch inventory has been disclosed in every filing since FY2024: $548.1M (LLY:10k_FY2024.md p.75), $601.4M (LLY:companies/LLY/10q_2025Q1.md p.15), $808.5M (10q_2025Q2 p.18), $952.3M (10q_2025Q3 p.18), $1.5B (LLY:10k_FY2025.md p.70). Analysts raised it on-record twice: Courtney Breen (AllianceBernstein) on Q3 2025 (grade B) estimated 'enough doses to support at least 5 million patients for a full year based on the inventory already built' (LLY:transcripts/2025Q3_transcript.md p.1), and again on Q1 2026 (grade D) cited 'extreme amounts of inventory pre-prepared for the launch' (LLY:transcripts/2026Q1_transcript.md p.1), answered with the 40-country international rollout. Output growth (1.8x doses) is in Q4 2025 prepared remarks (LLY:transcripts/2025Q4_transcript.md p.1). Receivable growth fits Patrik Jonsson's 'initial stocking in those markets where we launched' (Q3 2025, grade B) and Q2 2026 'there is an inventory build in the beginning' (LLY:transcripts/2026Q2_transcript.md p.1). The 'at risk' framing is stale: Foundayo was approved in April 2026 (Lilly press release LLY:policy/press_2026-04-09_foundayo_launch_pricing.md p.1), the 2026 10-Q inventory notes no longer carry a pre-launch line (LLY:10q_2026Q2.md p.15), and mid-2026 inventory growth (+52.5%) is close to Q2 revenue growth (+47.7%). CORRECTION: Narrow to the WIP mix: work in process went from $3,979M to $8,183M in 2025 and $9,997M by June 2026 (LLY:10q_2026Q2.md p.15), about 60% of inventory. skeptic_obviousness.round2: refuted=False severity=major. Settled the question the coordinator raised. I searched all 10 Lilly transcripts in the index (2024Q1-2025Q2 grade C; 2025Q3 B; 2025Q4 C; 2026Q1 D; 2026Q2 C) for days of inventory, inventory days, working capital and receivables: no Lilly speaker or analyst ever states an inventory-days level, a WIP figure or a receivables-vs-revenue gap. What is said on the record is the headline build: 1.8x incretin doses in 2025 (LLY:transcripts/2025Q4_transcript.md p.1), Breen's '5 million patients ... inventory already built' (LLY:transcripts/2025Q3_transcript.md p.1), and 'extreme amounts of inventory pre-prepared' (LLY:transcripts/2026Q1_transcript.md p.1). Pre-launch inventory is disclosed in every 10-Q. So the market knows inventory is large but has not been handed the ratio. The materiality skeptic's DIO excluding pre-launch stock, (13,744 - 1,500)/11,052 x 365 = 404 vs 329 days (10-K p.57, p.59, p.70), removes the part that was most said (the orforglipron stock) and still shows a jump. That is a ratio a press-release skim would not produce. I reverse my round 1 kill for that narrowed claim. Receivables are a different story: AR 20,083 vs 14,170 (+41.7%) against Q2 revenue +47.7% (10-Q 2026Q2 p.5, p.7) means the gap reversed by mid-2026, and Jonsson's launch-stocking remark explains it. CORRECTION: Inventory days rose from 329 to about 404 in 2025 even excluding the $1.5B orforglipron pre-launch stock, and WIP doubled to $8.2B ($10.0B by June 2026, about 60% of inventory). No call or release states either. Drop the receivables leg (reversed by mid-2026) and the pre-launch write-off downside (Foundayo approved April 2026).

verdict_reason: Lilly's inventory kept outgrowing cost of sales after orforglipron (Foundayo) was approved: inventory days on annualized quarterly cost of sales rose from about 410 at June 30, 2025 to about 469 at June 30, 2026 (inventory $11.0B to $16.8B, +52.5%, vs Q2 cost of sales +33.5%), with work in process at $10.0B or 60% of inventory. That is about $2.1B more inventory than year-ago days imply. The 2025 year-end build points the same way (about 305 to 404 days with pre-launch stock excluded at both ends). This is a cash and write-down-risk item, not an EPS item today. | Round 2 left both skeptics holding a narrowed inventory-days finding but disagreeing on the version and on whether it is material. I opened the pages. June version: inventories 16,793 (LLY:10q_2026Q2.md p.7) on Q2 cost of sales 3,268 (p.5) gives 468.9 days; 11,013.8 (LLY:companies/LLY/10q_2025Q2.md p.7) on 2,447.8 (p.5) gives 410.6 days. WIP is 9,997 of 16,793, or 59.5% (LLY:10q_2026Q2.md p.15), and that note has no pre-launch line after approval. At 410.6 days the inventory would be $14.7B, so the excess is $2.09B. Year-end version: 13,744 and 11,052 (LLY:10k_FY2025.md p.59, p.57) give 453.9 days, against 329.1 for 2024. The obviousness skeptic's 404 removes the $1.5B pre-launch stock (LLY:10k_FY2025.md p.70) from 2025 only. Removing the $548.1M at YE2024 too (LLY:10k_FY2024.md p.75) gives 305 to 404, a larger rise on a like-for-like basis. Likewise the June 2025 base includes $808.5M of pre-launch stock (LLY:companies/LLY/10q_2025Q2.md p.18), so 410 to 469 is the conservative form (380 to 469 ex-pre-launch). Ruling: I adopt the June 2026 version as the headline. It is post-approval, so the most-discussed part of the build (orforglipron pre-launch stock) cannot explain it, and that answers the obviousness skeptic's own concern. Dropped legs, which both skeptics conceded: receivables (AR +41.7% vs Q2 revenue +47.7% at June 2026, LLY:10q_2026Q2.md p.5, p.7) and the $1.5B write-off downside, stale after approval. On materiality I side with the materiality skeptic: confirmed as cash and working-capital (about 10% of FY2025 net income), and there is no EPS effect unless written down. On obviousness I side with the obviousness skeptic: the direction (a large build, 1.8x doses) is said, but neither skeptic found the days level or the WIP share stated in any indexed call or release. That is unrefuted, not confirmed. UNRESOLVED: (1) Materiality: the materiality skeptic holds that a cash-only working-capital build with no EPS effect may not meet the case's materiality test. The obviousness skeptic treats it as a major survivor. I rate it medium, not high, and leave open whether a cash item counts. (2) 'Never stated' rests on indexed transcripts that are grade C/D for Q4 2025 through Q2 2026, so it is unrefuted rather than confirmed.
